title: Verghese Kurien — I Too Had A Dream

topics.title: Verghese Kurien and the White Revolution

learn.hook: India once did not have enough milk for its children. Today it produces more milk than any other country. Who dreamed this big?
points: The lesson tells the story of Dr Verghese Kurien, whose dream was to make dairy farmers prosper. 'I Too Had a Dream' is also the title of his memoir.
Verghese Kurien was born on 26 November 1921 in Kozhikode (Calicut), Kerala. In 1949 he was posted to Anand in Gujarat, where he chose to stay and work with dairy farmers.
He is called the 'Father of the White Revolution'. The White Revolution was the huge rise in India's milk production.
Operation Flood, launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) under his leadership, linked village milk producers to cities across India. Kurien was the first chairman of the NDDB.
Today India is the world's largest producer of milk, and his birthday, 26 November, is celebrated as National Milk Day.

example.q: Read this original passage: 'Kurien was an engineer, not a farmer. Yet when he saw how farmers in Anand got very little money for their milk, he decided to stay and help them. He believed that if farmers owned their own dairy, they would get a fair price.' Think it through: what was Kurien's dream?
steps: Notice the problem: farmers got very little money for their milk.
Notice his decision: he stayed in Anand to help them.
Notice his belief: farmers should own their dairy to get a fair price.
So his dream was about fairness and farmers' prosperity.
example.answer: His dream was that dairy farmers would own and run their own dairies and get a fair price for their milk.

learn.reallife: The packet of milk or curd that reaches your home every morning is part of a supply chain that grew out of the White Revolution.

quiz.q: Who is known as the 'Father of the White Revolution' in India?
quiz.explain: Verghese Kurien led India's dairy revolution. M. S. Swaminathan is linked with the Green Revolution.
steps: Verghese Kurien led India's dairy (milk) revolution.
M. S. Swaminathan is linked with the Green Revolution.
Answer: Verghese Kurien
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the White Revolution (milk) with the Green Revolution (grains)

quiz.q: The White Revolution is linked with a big increase in the production of ___.
quiz.explain: 'White' stands for milk. Fish is the Blue Revolution and wheat is linked with the Green Revolution.
steps: 'White' in White Revolution stands for milk.
Fish is the Blue Revolution; wheat is the Green Revolution.
Answer: milk

quiz.q: When is National Milk Day celebrated in India?
quiz.explain: It is celebrated on 26 November, Verghese Kurien's birthday. (1 June is World Milk Day.)
steps: National Milk Day honours Kurien on his birthday.
It is 26 November (1 June is World Milk Day).
Answer: 26 November
quiz.mistake: Confuses National Milk Day with World Milk Day

quiz.q: In which state was Verghese Kurien born?
quiz.explain: He was born in Kozhikode, Kerala, though his life's work was in Anand, Gujarat.
steps: Kurien was born in Kozhikode.
Kozhikode is in Kerala (his work was later in Anand, Gujarat).
Answer: Kerala

quiz.q: Operation Flood was launched in which year?
quiz.explain: The NDDB launched Operation Flood in 1970.
steps: Operation Flood was launched by the NDDB.
It began in 1970.
Answer: 1970
quiz.mistake: Guesses a famous year without recalling the fact

quiz.q: Read: 'Kurien was an engineer, not a farmer. Yet he decided to stay and help the farmers of Anand.' The word 'Yet' shows ___.
quiz.explain: 'Yet' means 'but still'. It contrasts his engineering training with his choice to work with farmers.
steps: 'Yet' means 'but still'.
It contrasts his engineering training with his choice to help farmers — a contrast.
Answer: a contrast

quiz.q: Which word means 'to become successful and well-off'?

'Proper', 'prosecute' and 'protect' only look similar.

learn.hook: What happens when thousands of farmers who each own just one or two buffaloes join hands? They build one of India's biggest dairies!
points: A cooperative is a group owned and run by its members for their shared benefit. Each member has a say (one member, one vote) and profits are shared among members.
In 1946, dairy farmers of Kaira (Kheda) district formed the Kaira District Cooperative Milk Producers' Union at Anand, Gujarat, led by Tribhuvandas Patel. Its products later took the brand name Amul.
Amul is often explained as 'Anand Milk Union Limited'. Kurien worked with this union and helped it grow.
The 'Anand pattern' has three levels: village dairy cooperative societies collect milk, a district union processes it, and a state federation markets it.
Because the farmers own the system, middlemen are removed and farmers receive a fairer price for their milk.

example.q: Read this original passage: 'Every morning and evening, Lakshmiben carries her buffalo's milk to the village society. The milk is tested for fat, and she is paid according to its quality. At the end of the year, she also gets a share of the profit, because she is a member.' Think it through: why is this a cooperative?
steps: Lakshmiben is a member, not just a seller.
She is paid fairly, by the quality of her milk.
Profits are shared with members like her.
Ownership and benefit belong to the members: that is a cooperative.
example.answer: It is a cooperative because the farmers are members who own it, are paid fairly and share its profits.

learn.reallife: Housing societies in cities, many sugar mills in Maharashtra, and cooperative banks in towns are also cooperatives run by their members.

quiz.q: What is a cooperative?
options: A company owned by one rich person
A group owned and run by its members for their shared benefit
A shop that sells only milk
quiz.explain: In a cooperative, the members are the owners and share the benefits.

It is run by its members for their shared benefit.
Answer: A group owned and run by its members for their shared benefit

quiz.q: The Kaira District Cooperative Milk Producers' Union was formed in 1946 in which town?
quiz.explain: The union was formed at Anand in Kaira (Kheda) district, Gujarat.
steps: The Kaira District Cooperative Milk Producers' Union was formed in 1946.
It was formed at Anand, Kaira (Kheda) district, Gujarat.
Answer: Anand
quiz.mistake: Guesses a large city instead of the dairy town

quiz.q: Which farmers' leader led the Kaira union at Anand?
quiz.explain: Tribhuvandas Patel led the farmers' union and persuaded Kurien to stay on and help it.
steps: Tribhuvandas Patel led the Kaira farmers' union at Anand.
He persuaded Kurien to stay on and help it.
Answer: Tribhuvandas Patel
quiz.mistake: Picks another famous Indian name

quiz.q: In the Anand pattern, who collects milk directly from the farmers?
quiz.explain: The village society is the first level. It collects and tests the milk from member farmers.
steps: The Anand pattern has levels; the first is the village.
The village dairy cooperative society collects and tests milk from farmers.
Answer: The village dairy cooperative society
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the three levels of the Anand pattern

quiz.q: Read: 'At the end of the year, Lakshmiben also gets a share of the profit, because she is a member.' Why does she get a share?
options: She is a member of the cooperative
She sold the most milk in India
quiz.explain: The passage says she gets a share because she is a member. Members share the profits.
steps: The passage gives the reason directly: 'because she is a member'.
Members share the cooperative's profit.
Answer: She is a member of the cooperative
quiz.mistake: Ignores the reason given in the sentence

quiz.q: How does a cooperative help farmers get a fairer price?
quiz.explain: Members sell through their own system, so the money does not go to middlemen.
steps: Farmers sell through their own cooperative system.
This removes middlemen, so more money reaches the farmers.
Answer: By removing middlemen
quiz.mistake: Does not see the role of middlemen in lowering farmers' income

quiz.q: The prefix 'co-' in 'cooperative' means ___.
quiz.explain: 'Co-' means together, as in co-operate (work together), co-author and co-pilot.
steps: The prefix 'co-' appears in co-operate, co-author, co-pilot.
It means together.
Answer: together
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'co-' with 'counter-' (against)

quiz.q: Which of these is a cooperative?
options: A housing society run by its residents
A shop owned by one family
quiz.explain: A housing society is owned and managed by its member residents.
steps: A cooperative is owned and managed by its members.
A housing society run by its residents is such a body; a family shop is privately owned.
Answer: A housing society run by its residents
quiz.mistake: Thinks any group of people working together is a cooperative

teach.praise: Hooray! In a cooperative, the members own it together and share the profit fairly, just like the dairy farmers of Anand!
teach.nudge: Who owns a cooperative? And what happens to the money it earns?

revise.summary: A cooperative is owned and run by its members for their shared benefit. In 1946 Kaira dairy farmers, led by Tribhuvandas Patel, formed a union at Anand whose products became Amul, and the Anand pattern removes middlemen.
focus: Define a cooperative: one member, one vote, shared profits.
Know the three levels of the Anand pattern.
Explain how cooperatives give farmers a fairer price.
remember: A cooperative is a group owned and run by its members for their shared benefit.
Anand pattern: village societies collect milk, a district union processes it, a state federation markets it.
Amul is often explained as 'Anand Milk Union Limited'.
traps: Not every business or group working together is a cooperative; members must own it.
Don't mix up the three levels: the village society collects milk from farmers.

topics.title: Describing a process: active and passive voice

learn.hook: 'The farmer milks the buffalo' or 'The buffalo is milked'? Both are correct. The choice depends on what you want to highlight.
points: In the active voice, the subject does the action: The society collects the milk.
In the passive voice, the receiver of the action becomes the subject: The milk is collected by the society.
Passive = a form of 'be' + past participle. Present: is/are collected. Past: was/were collected. Future: will be collected. Present continuous: is being collected. With modals: can be collected.
The doer is shown with 'by' (by the society), or left out when it is unknown or unimportant: The milk is pasteurised and packed.
The passive is common when describing processes, because the steps matter more than who does them.

example.q: Think it through: Change to the passive voice: 'The workers packed the milk in pouches.'
steps: Object of the active sentence: the milk. It becomes the subject.
The verb 'packed' is simple past, so use was/were + past participle: was packed.
Add the doer with 'by': by the workers.
Keep the rest: in pouches.
example.answer: The milk was packed in pouches by the workers.

learn.reallife: Instructions and science textbooks often use the passive: 'The solution is heated', 'The seeds are sown in June'.

games.title: Active or passive?
items: The farmer milks the cow.
The milk is tested for fat.
Kurien built a strong cooperative.
The butter was made in Anand.
The children drink milk daily.
The pouches are sealed by a machine.
The truck carries the milk.
Ghee will be sold at the fair.

quiz.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: Milk is sold by the farmer.
quiz.explain: 'Is sold' (be + past participle) with the receiver 'milk' as subject is passive.
steps: Passive = form of 'be' + past participle, with the receiver as subject.
'Milk is sold by the farmer' fits that pattern.
Answer: Milk is sold by the farmer.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any sentence with 'is' is passive

quiz.q: Change to passive: 'The society tests the milk.'
options: The milk is tested by the society.
The milk was tested by the society.
The society is tested by the milk.
quiz.explain: Present tense 'tests' becomes 'is tested', and the object 'the milk' becomes the subject.
steps: Make the object 'the milk' the subject.
Present 'tests' → 'is tested': The milk is tested by the society.
Answer: The milk is tested by the society.
quiz.mistake: Changes the tense while changing the voice

quiz.q: Change to passive: 'Kurien wrote a memoir.'
options: A memoir is written by Kurien.
A memoir was wrote by Kurien.
A memoir was written by Kurien.
A memoir has been write by Kurien.
quiz.explain: Simple past 'wrote' becomes 'was written', using the past participle 'written'.
steps: Simple past 'wrote' becomes 'was' + past participle.
The past participle of write is 'written': A memoir was written by Kurien.
Answer: A memoir was written by Kurien.
quiz.mistake: Uses the past tense 'wrote' instead of the past participle 'written'

quiz.q: Complete in the passive: 'The milk ___ to Mumbai tomorrow.'
quiz.explain: 'Tomorrow' is future, and passive future is will be + past participle.
steps: 'Tomorrow' shows future time.
Future passive = will be + past participle: will be sent.
Answer: will be sent
quiz.mistake: Uses the active form or the wrong tense

quiz.q: In 'The cheese was made by the cooperative', who did the action?
quiz.explain: In a passive sentence, the doer comes after 'by'.
steps: In a passive sentence the doer comes after 'by'.
Here 'by the cooperative', so the cooperative did the action.
Answer: the cooperative
quiz.mistake: Thinks the subject of a passive sentence is the doer

quiz.q: Why is the passive often used to describe a process?
options: The steps matter more than who does them
quiz.explain: In processes, what happens to the milk matters more than which worker does it.
steps: In a process, what happens matters more than who does it.
The passive keeps the focus on the steps.
Answer: The steps matter more than who does them
quiz.mistake: Thinks the passive is chosen because it is shorter

quiz.q: Change to active: 'The calves are fed by Raju.'
options: Raju is fed by the calves.
quiz.explain: The doer 'Raju' becomes the subject, and present passive 'are fed' becomes present active 'feeds'.
steps: Make the doer 'Raju' the subject.
Present passive 'are fed' → present active 'feeds': Raju feeds the calves.
Answer: Raju feeds the calves.
quiz.mistake: Changes the tense or swaps the doer and receiver wrongly

quiz.q: Choose the correct passive form: 'The milk ___ right now.'
quiz.explain: 'Right now' needs the present continuous; in the passive that is is being + past participle.
steps: 'Right now' needs the present continuous.
Present continuous passive = is being + past participle: is being pasteurised.
Answer: is being pasteurised
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 'being' in the present continuous passive

teach.ask: Gappu tilts his head: 'The worm was eaten.' Who ate it? How is a passive sentence different from an active one?
teach.praise: Gulp! In the passive, the receiver becomes the subject and we use 'be' plus the past participle. The doer comes with 'by', or is left out!
teach.nudge: In a passive sentence, is the subject the doer or the receiver? Which verb parts do we use?

revise.summary: In the active voice the subject does the action; in the passive the receiver becomes the subject. The passive (be + past participle) is common in describing processes because the steps matter more than who does them.
focus: Change active to passive and back without changing the tense.
Use the right passive form for each tense.
Know when to leave out the doer.
remember: Passive = a form of 'be' + past participle.
is/are collected; was/were collected; will be collected; is being collected; can be collected.
The doer is shown with 'by', or left out when unknown or unimportant.
traps: Don't change the tense while changing the voice.
Don't use the past tense instead of the past participle: 'was written', not 'was wrote'.
Don't forget 'being' in the present continuous passive: 'is being pasteurised'.
